es.summary: Diseminación de células cancerosas desde el tumor primario a órganos distantes mediante sangre o linfa.
key_points: Es la causa principal de estadios avanzados y mortalidad en cáncer.
Se evalúa con el sistema TNM (M = metástasis).
Los síntomas dependen del órgano metastásico.
El tratamiento es sistémico y paliativo.

pathophysiology: Células tumorales pierden adhesión y penetran la membrana basal.
Intravasan al torrente sanguíneo o linfático y sobreviven al flujo.
Se adhieren a endotelio distal, extravasan y forman micro‑metástasis.
Inducen angiogénesis para obtener nutrientes y crecer.
Proliferan formando nuevos tumores en órganos distantes.
risk_factors: Tumor primario de alto grado o tamaño grande.
Inmunosupresión o terapia previa que favorece diseminación.
signs_symptoms: Síntomas específicos: disnea (pulmón), ictericia (hígado), déficit neurológico (cerebro).
diagnostics: Tomografía axial computarizada (TAC) o resonancia magnética (RM) para localizar lesiones.
PET‑CT para detección de actividad metabólica en metástasis.
Biopsia de lesión distante para confirmar histología.
Marcadores tumorales séricos (CEA, CA‑125) pueden estar elevados.
treatment: Terapia dirigida (p. ej. trastuzumab) o inmunoterapia.
Radioterapia paliativa para control del dolor y sangrado.
Cirugía metastásica selectiva (p. ej. resección hepática).
Cuidados paliativos y manejo del dolor.
nursing_care: Evaluar dolor, nivel de conciencia y signos vitales cada 4 h.
Monitorear balance hídrico y peso diario.
Administrar quimioterapia y antieméticos según prescripción.
Preparar al paciente para estudios de imagen (ayuda para movilidad).
Proveer medidas de confort: posición semisentado, control de temperatura.
patient_teaching: Explicar la naturaleza de la metástasis y objetivo del tratamiento.
Enseñar signos de alarma: aumento de dolor, fiebre, dificultad respiratoria.
Importancia de la nutrición alta en proteínas y control de hidratación.
Adherencia a la terapia y citas de seguimiento.
Disponibilidad de apoyo psicológico y grupos de pacientes.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de déficit de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Balance hídrico: ingesta ≥1500 mL/día en 48 h

interventions.action: Evaluar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada turno.
interventions.rationale: Detectar desequilibrio temprano y guiar reposición.

interventions.action: Ofrecer líquidos entre comidas y registrar volumen.
interventions.rationale: Facilita cumplimiento de metas de hidratación.

interventions.action: Administrar antieméticos antes de la quimioterapia.
interventions.rationale: Reduce náuseas y mejora la ingesta oral.

interventions.action: Colaborar con nutricionista para plan de alta energía.
interventions.rationale: Previene pérdida de peso y déficit de líquidos.

interventions.action: Monitorear signos de deshidratación (turgencia, mucosas).

outcomes: Cultivos: negativos en ausencia de síntomas

interventions.action: Realizar higiene de manos antes y después de contacto.
Inspeccionar piel y sitio de catéter cada turno.
Mantener técnica aséptica al manipular dispositivos invasivos.
Educar al paciente sobre signos de infección (fiebre, enrojecimiento).
Administrar profilaxis antibiótica según orden médica.

en.summary: Dissemination of cancerous cells from the primary tumor to distant organs via blood or lymph.
key_points: It is the main cause of advanced stages and mortality in cancer.
It is evaluated with the TNM system (M = metastasis).
Symptoms depend on the metastatic organ.

pathophysiology: Tumor cells lose adhesion and penetrate the basement membrane.
They intravasate into the bloodstream or lymphatic system and survive the flow.
They adhere to distal endothelium, extravasate, and form micrometastases.
They induce angiogenesis to obtain nutrients and grow.
They proliferate forming new tumors in distant organs.
risk_factors: Immunosuppression or prior therapy that favors dissemination.
signs_symptoms: Localized pain depending on affected organ.
Specific symptoms: dyspnea (lung), jaundice (liver), neurological deficit (brain).
diagnostics: CT scan or MRI to locate lesions.
PET‑CT for detection of metabolic activity in metastases.
Biopsy of distant lesion to confirm histology.
Serum tumor markers (CEA, CA‑125) may be elevated.
treatment: Systemic chemotherapy based on histologic type.
Palliative radiotherapy for pain and bleeding control.
complications: Deep venous thrombosis due to hypercoagulability.
nursing_care: Assess pain, level of consciousness, and vital signs every 4 h.
Monitor fluid balance and daily weight.
Administer chemotherapy and antiemetics as prescribed.
Prepare the patient for imaging studies (mobility assistance).
Provide comfort measures: semi‑upright position, temperature control.
patient_teaching: Explain the nature of metastasis and treatment goals.
Teach warning signs: increased pain, fever, breathing difficulty.
Importance of high-protein nutrition and hydration control.
Adherence to therapy and follow-up appointments.
Availability of psychological support and patient groups.

outcomes: Fluid balance: intake ≥1500 mL/day in 48 h

interventions.action: Assess fluid intake and output each shift.
interventions.rationale: Detect early imbalance and guide replacement.

interventions.action: Offer fluids between meals and record volume.
Administer antiemetics before chemotherapy.
interventions.rationale: Reduces nausea and improves oral intake.

interventions.action: Collaborate with dietitian for high‑energy plan.
interventions.rationale: Prevents weight loss and fluid deficit.

interventions.action: Monitor signs of dehydration (turgor, mucous membranes).

outcomes: Cultures: negative in absence of symptoms

interventions.action: Perform hand hygiene before and after contact.
Inspect skin and catheter site each shift.
Maintain aseptic technique when handling invasive devices.
Educate patient on infection signs (fever, redness).
Administer antibiotic prophylaxis per order.

key_points.1.quote: The basic TNM system (tumor, node, and metastasis ) represents the anatomic extent of solid tumors, and it gauges the size and extent of tumor (T), lymph node involvement (N), and systemic involvement or metastasis (M) for prognostic implications.

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: metastasis: cancerous cells can spread, usually via the bloodstream or lymphatic system ( Figure 31.3 )

sections.pathophysiology.3.quote: angiogenesis: cancerous cells can form their own network of blood vessels to obtain needed nutrients and oxygen and to allow tumor cells to leave the primary tumor site

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: Examples of oncogenes include the following: HER2 (certain breast cancers) KRAS (colorectal or pancreatic cancer) ABL1 (chronic myeloid leukemia) EGFR (lung cancer and glioblastoma)

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Symptoms include localized bone pain, swelling, and possible fractures without traumatic injury.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Weight loss is a common manifestation of cancer.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: Fatigue is the most frequently reported manifestation, affecting as many as 91 percent of patients (NCI, 2024b).

sections.diagnostics.2.quote: A biopsy is the most reliable method to confirm a cancer diagnosis.

sections.treatment.0.quote: Treatment depends on the type of cancer and how advanced it is.

sections.treatment.1.quote: Therapies for hematological cancers include chemotherapy medications, targeted drug therapies, immunotherapy , radiation therapy to the bone marrow (often affecting the central nervous system), or a stem cell transplant to reestablish healthy bone marrow.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: The spread of cancer from one part of the body to another is called metastasis.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Solid and site-specific tumors, usually have symptoms of pain, lumps, swelling, skin changes, difficulty breathing, difficulty swallowing, changes in bowel or bladder habits, the appearance of blood in stool or urine, or persistent cough or voice changes.

sections.patient_teaching.4.quote: This includes accessing the correct treatments, symptom management, emotional and social supports, and maintaining or regaining physical and emotional health after treatment has ended.
